title: Section 144 — Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents
text:
subsection_1: text: If any person having sufficient means neglects or refuses to maintain— (a) his wife, unable to maintain herself; or (b) his legitimate or illegitimate child, whether married or not, unable to maintain itself; or (c) his legitimate or illegitimate child (not being a married daughter) who has attained majority, where such child is, by reason of any physical or mental abnormality or injury unable to maintain itself; or (d) his father or mother, unable to maintain himself or herself, a Magistrate of the first class may, upon proof of such neglect or refusal, order such person to make a monthly allowance for the maintenance of his wife or such child, father or mother, at such monthly rate as such Magistrate thinks fit and to pay the same to such person as the Magistrate may from time to time direct.
provisos: Provided that the Magistrate may order the father of a female child referred to in clause (b) to make such allowance, until she attains her majority, if the Magistrate is satisfied that the husband of such female child, if married, is not possessed of sufficient means.
Provided further that the Magistrate may, during the pendency of the proceeding regarding monthly allowance for the maintenance under this sub-section, order such person to make a monthly allowance for the interim maintenance of his wife or such child, father or mother, and the expenses of such proceeding which the Magistrate considers reasonable, and to pay the same to such person as the Magistrate may from time to time direct.

title: Section 144 — Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents
text:
Provided also that an application for the monthly allowance for the interim maintenance and expenses of proceeding under the second proviso shall, as far as possible, be disposed of within sixty days from the date of the service of notice of the application to such person.
explanation: For the purposes of this Chapter, “wife” includes a woman who has been divorced by, or has obtained a divorce from, her husband and has not remarried.
subsection_2: Any such allowance for the maintenance or interim maintenance and expenses of proceeding shall be payable from the date of the order, or, if so ordered, from the date of the application for maintenance or interim maintenance and expenses of proceeding, as the case may be.
subsection_3: text: If any person so ordered fails without sufficient cause to comply with the order, any such Magistrate may, for every breach of the order, issue a warrant for levying the amount due in the manner provided for levying fines, and may sentence such person, for the whole or any part of each month's allowance for the maintenance or the interim maintenance and expenses of proceeding, as the case may be, remaining unpaid after the execution of the warrant, to imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month or until payment if sooner made.
provisos: Provided that no warrant shall be issued for the recovery of any amount due under this section unless application be made to the Court to levy such amount within a period of one year from the date on which it became due.

title: Section 144 — Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents
text:
Provided further that if such person offers to maintain his wife on condition of her living with him, and she refuses to live with him, such Magistrate may consider any grounds of refusal stated by her, and may make an order under this section notwithstanding such offer, if he is satisfied that there is just ground for so doing.
explanation: If a husband has contracted marriage with another woman or keeps a mistress, it shall be considered to be just ground for his wife's refusal to live with him.
subsection_4: No wife shall be entitled to receive an allowance for the maintenance or the interim maintenance and expenses of proceeding, from her husband under this section if she is living in adultery, or if, without any sufficient reason, she refuses to live with her husband, or if they are living separately by mutual consent.
subsection_5: On proof that any wife in whose favour an order has been made under this section is living in adultery, or that without sufficient reason she refuses to live with her husband, or that they are living separately by mutual consent, the Magistrate shall cancel the order.

title: Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 — Section 18
text:
subject: Maintenance of a Hindu wife
scope: Section 18
chapter: Chapter III — Maintenance
important_note: Section 18 concerns the entitlement of a Hindu wife to maintenance from her husband and circumstances in which she may live separately without forfeiting her claim.

title: Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 — Section 18
text:
title: Maintenance of wife
statutory_text: subsection_1: Subject to the provisions of this section, a Hindu wife, whether married before or after the commencement of this Act, shall be entitled to be maintained by her husband during her lifetime.
subsection_2: intro: A Hindu wife shall be entitled to live separately from her husband without forfeiting her claim to maintenance if:
grounds: a: He is guilty of desertion, that is to say, of abandoning her without reasonable cause and without her consent or against her wish, or of wilfully neglecting her.
b: He has treated her with such cruelty as to cause a reasonable apprehension in her mind that it will be harmful or injurious to live with her husband.
d: He has any other wife living.
e: He keeps a concubine in the same house in which his wife is living or habitually resides with a concubine elsewhere.
f: He has ceased to be a Hindu by conversion to another religion.
g: There is any other cause justifying her living separately.
omitted_clause: Clause (c) has been omitted.
subsection_3: A Hindu wife shall not be entitled to separate residence and maintenance from her husband if she is unchaste or ceases to be a Hindu by conversion to another religion.
plain_summary: Section 18 provides that, subject to the section's conditions, a Hindu wife is entitled to maintenance from her husband during her lifetime. It also recognizes specified circumstances in which she may live separately without losing her maintenance claim.
key_elements: The provision applies to a Hindu wife.
The wife is entitled to be maintained by her husband during her lifetime, subject to the section.
A wife may live separately without forfeiting her maintenance claim in specified circumstances.
Desertion is one recognized ground.

Conversion of the husband to another religion is one recognized ground.
Any other cause justifying separate residence is one recognized ground.

title: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 — Sections 24 and 25
text:
subject: Maintenance and alimony under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
scope: Sections 24 and 25
important_note: These sections provide statutory routes within proceedings under the Hindu Marriage Act. They do not establish a universal fixed percentage or mathematical formula for maintenance.

title: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 — Sections 24 and 25
text:
section_24: title: Maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceedings
type: interim_maintenance
plain_summary: Where, in a proceeding under the Hindu Marriage Act, either the wife or husband has no independent income sufficient for their support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding, the court may, on application by either spouse, order the respondent to pay proceeding expenses and a reasonable monthly sum during the proceeding, having regard to the petitioner's own income and the respondent's income.
statutory_text: main_provision: Where in any proceeding under this Act it appears to the court that either the wife or the husband, as the case may be, has no independent income sufficient for her or his support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding, it may, on the application of the wife or the husband, order the respondent to pay to the petitioner the expenses of the proceeding, and monthly during the proceeding such sum as, having regard to the petitioner's own income and the income of the respondent, it may seem to the court to be reasonable.
proviso: Provided that the application for the payment of the expenses of the proceeding and such monthly sum during the proceeding, shall, as far as possible, be disposed of within sixty days from the date of service of notice on the wife or the husband, as the case may be.
key_elements: Applies to proceedings under the Hindu Marriage Act.
Either spouse may apply.
The applicant's independent income is relevant.
The respondent's income is relevant.
The court may order payment of expenses of the proceeding.
The court may order a monthly sum during the proceeding.
The amount is what the court considers reasonable having regard to the relevant income.

title: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 — Sections 24 and 25
text:
The application should, as far as possible, be disposed of within sixty days from the date of service of notice.

Ask for relevant income information of both spouses.

section_25: title: Permanent alimony and maintenance
type: permanent_alimony
plain_summary: A court exercising jurisdiction under the Hindu Marriage Act may, at the time of passing a decree or subsequently, on an application by either spouse, order the respondent to pay maintenance and support as a gross sum or monthly or periodical sum for a term not exceeding the life of the applicant, having regard to the statutory considerations and circumstances of the case.
statutory_text: subsection_1: Any court exercising jurisdiction under this Act may, at the time of passing any decree or at any time subsequent thereto, on application made to it for the purpose by either the wife or the husband, as the case may be, order that the respondent shall pay to the applicant for her or his maintenance and support such gross sum or such monthly or periodical sum for a term not exceeding the life of the applicant as, having regard to the respondent's own income and other property, if any, the income and other property of the applicant, the conduct of the parties and other circumstances of the case, it may seem to the court to be just, and any such payment may be secured, if necessary, by a charge on the immovable property of the respondent.

title: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 — Sections 24 and 25
text:
subsection_2: If the court is satisfied that there is a change in the circumstances of either party at any time after it has made an order under sub-section (1), it may at the instance of either party, vary, modify or rescind any such order in such manner as the court may deem just.
subsection_3: If the court is satisfied that the party in whose favour an order has been made under this section has re-married or, if such party is the wife, that she has not remained chaste, or, if such party is the husband, that he has had sexual intercourse with any woman outside wedlock, it may at the instance of the other party vary, modify or rescind any such order in such manner as the court may deem just.

The application may be made at the time of passing a decree or subsequently.

The applicant's income and other property may be considered.

Other circumstances of the case may be considered.

title: Mohd Abdul Samad v. State of Telangana & Anr.
text:
subject: Maintenance rights of a divorced Muslim woman
important_note: The Supreme Court considered whether a divorced Muslim woman can seek maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and addressed the relationship between that remedy and the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986.

title: Mohd Abdul Samad v. State of Telangana & Anr.
text:
issue: Whether a divorced Muslim woman can claim maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
holding: A divorced Muslim woman can seek maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. The Supreme Court held that the remedy under Section 125 is available to a divorced Muslim woman and is not excluded merely because she is governed by the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986.
important_principles: A divorced Muslim woman can invoke the maintenance remedy under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
The remedy under Section 125 CrPC is a secular remedy and is not confined by the personal law of the parties.
The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986 does not take away the remedy available to a divorced Muslim woman under Section 125 CrPC.
The availability of a remedy under the 1986 Act does not by itself prevent a divorced Muslim woman from seeking maintenance under Section 125 CrPC.
The judgment emphasizes the protective purpose of maintenance provisions and the need to prevent destitution and vagrancy.

text:
subject: Free legal services, legal aid eligibility and access
purpose: Provide reliable information about legal services, free legal aid, eligibility and access to Legal Services Institutions.
important_note: This source provides information about accessing legal services. It must not be used by the AI to determine the outcome of a user's legal case.

definition: Legal services include services connected with the conduct of a case or other legal proceeding before a court, authority or tribunal, as well as advice on legal matters.
free_legal_aid_may_include: Representation by an advocate in legal proceedings.

title: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 — Section 20
text:
subject: Monetary reliefs arising from domestic violence
scope: Section 20
chapter: Chapter IV — Procedure for obtaining orders of reliefs
important_note: Section 20 allows the Magistrate to direct monetary relief to meet expenses incurred and losses suffered by the aggrieved person and any child as a result of domestic violence.

title: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 — Section 20
text:
title: Monetary reliefs
statutory_text: subsection_1: intro: While disposing of an application under sub-section (1) of section 12, the Magistrate may direct the respondent to pay monetary relief to meet the expenses incurred and losses suffered by the aggrieved person and any child of the aggrieved person as a result of the domestic violence.
included_reliefs: a: Loss of earnings.
b: Medical expenses.
c: Loss caused due to the destruction, damage or removal of any property from the control of the aggrieved person.
d: Maintenance for the aggrieved person as well as her children, if any, including an order under or in addition to an order of maintenance under section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 or any other law for the time being in force.
subsection_2: The monetary relief granted under this section shall be adequate, fair and reasonable and consistent with the standard of living to which the aggrieved person is accustomed.
subsection_3: The Magistrate shall have the power to order an appropriate lump sum payment or monthly payments of maintenance, as the nature and circumstances of the case may require.
subsection_4: The Magistrate shall send a copy of the order for monetary relief made under sub-section (1) to the parties to the application and to the in charge of the police station within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the respondent resides.
subsection_5: The respondent shall pay the monetary relief granted to the aggrieved person within the period specified in the order under sub-section (1).

title: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 — Section 20
text:
subsection_6: Upon failure by the respondent to make payment in terms of the order under sub-section (1), the Magistrate may direct the employer or a debtor of the respondent to directly pay to the aggrieved person or deposit with the court a portion of the wages, salaries or debt due to or accrued to the credit of the respondent, which amount may be adjusted towards the monetary relief payable.
plain_summary: Section 20 provides a statutory route for monetary relief where domestic violence has resulted in expenses or losses. The relief may include loss of earnings, medical expenses, property-related losses, and maintenance for the aggrieved person and her children.
key_elements: The provision operates in connection with an application under section 12.
The Magistrate may direct the respondent to pay monetary relief.
Relief may address expenses incurred and losses suffered as a result of domestic violence.
Loss of earnings may be included.
Medical expenses may be included.
Loss caused by destruction, damage or removal of property may be included.
Maintenance for the aggrieved person and her children may be included.
Maintenance under or in addition to maintenance under another law may be covered.
Monetary relief should be adequate, fair and reasonable.
The relief should be consistent with the standard of living to which the aggrieved person is accustomed.
Maintenance may be ordered as a lump sum or through monthly payments.
The section also provides a mechanism concerning non-payment of ordered monetary relief.
rag_use: Identify Section 20 as a possible legal route where domestic violence facts are relevant.
Explain the types of monetary relief expressly recognized by the section.

title: Special Marriage Act, 1954 — Sections 36 and 37
text:
subject: Alimony pendente lite, permanent alimony and maintenance
scope: Sections 36 and 37
chapter: Chapter VII — Jurisdiction and Procedure
important_note: Sections 36 and 37 provide statutory routes for interim and permanent financial support in proceedings under Chapter V or Chapter VI of the Special Marriage Act.

title: Special Marriage Act, 1954 — Sections 36 and 37
text:
title: Alimony pendente lite
statutory_text: main: Where in any proceeding under Chapter V or Chapter VI it appears to the district court that the wife has no independent income sufficient for her support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding, it may, on the application of the wife, order the husband to pay to her the expenses of the proceeding, and weekly or monthly during the proceeding such sum as having regard to the husband's income, it may seem to the court to be reasonable.
proviso: Provided that the application for the payment of the expenses of the proceeding and such weekly or monthly sum during the proceeding under Chapter V or Chapter VI, shall, as far as possible, be disposed of within sixty days from the date of service of notice on the husband.
plain_summary: Section 36 allows the district court, in proceedings under Chapter V or VI, to order the husband to pay the wife's proceeding expenses and a reasonable weekly or monthly amount during the proceeding when she has no independent income sufficient for her support and necessary proceeding expenses.
key_elements: The proceeding must be under Chapter V or Chapter VI.
The provision applies where the wife has no independent income sufficient for her support and necessary proceeding expenses.
The wife may apply for relief under the section.
The court may order payment of expenses of the proceeding.
The court may order a weekly or monthly amount during the proceeding.
The amount is to be determined having regard to the husband's income and what appears reasonable to the court.
The application should, as far as possible, be disposed of within sixty days from service of notice on the husband.
rag_use: Identify Section 36 as a possible interim-support route in relevant Special Marriage Act proceedings.

title: Special Marriage Act, 1954 — Sections 36 and 37
text:
Explain the distinction between support during proceedings and permanent maintenance.
Retrieve the provision when a user's facts indicate lack of sufficient independent income and ongoing proceeding expenses.

title: Special Marriage Act, 1954 — Sections 36 and 37
text:
title: Permanent alimony and maintenance
statutory_text: subsection_1: Any court exercising jurisdiction under Chapter V or Chapter VI may, at the time of passing any decree or at any time subsequent to the decree, on application made to it for the purpose, order that the husband shall secure to the wife for her maintenance and support, if necessary, by a charge on the husband's property such gross sum or such monthly or periodical payment of money for a term not exceeding her life, as, having regard to her own property, if any, her husband's property and ability, the conduct of the parties and other circumstances of the case, it may seem to the court to be just.
subsection_2: If the district court is satisfied that there is a change in the circumstances of either party at any time after it has made an order under sub-section (1), it may, at the instance of either party, vary, modify or rescind any such order in such manner as it may seem to the court to be just.
plain_summary: Section 37 allows a court exercising jurisdiction under Chapter V or Chapter VI to order permanent alimony and maintenance for the wife at the time of a decree or after the decree. The court considers factors including the parties' property, the husband's ability, the conduct of the parties and other circumstances.
key_elements: The court must be exercising jurisdiction under Chapter V or Chapter VI.
An application may be made for permanent alimony and maintenance.
An order may be made when the decree is passed or after the decree.
The court may order a gross sum.
The court may order monthly or periodical payments.
The payment may be secured by a charge on the husband's property if necessary.
The term of payment cannot exceed the wife's life.
The court considers the wife's property, if any.

title: Special Marriage Act, 1954 — Sections 36 and 37
text:
The court considers the husband's property and ability.
The court considers the conduct of the parties.
The court may consider other circumstances of the case.
The district court may vary, modify or rescind the order when circumstances of either party change.
